Mage-Flow: An Efficient Native-Resolution Foundation Model for Image Generation and Editing

分类方向模型与训练方法 / 架构设计主题diffusion / generative modeling
Xinjie Zhang, Peng Zhang, Shicheng Zheng, Jinghao Guo, Zhaoyang Jia, Yifei Shen et al.
high · 2026-07-21

为什么值得看 这项工作直接面向高分辨率扩散生成的训练、部署和交互延迟瓶颈：通过潜变量编码器、原生分辨率扩散变换器与系统级内核融合的协同设计，把四十亿参数级模型的端到端训练吞吐提高约二点五倍，并将高分辨率生成和编辑压缩到少步推理；对关注低成本训练、单卡部署和实时图像编辑的研究者尤其有参考价值。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 57）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

大规模视觉生成模型的训练、微调、部署成本高，且高分辨率生成和编辑通常难以满足交互延迟要求。

02
方法

方法联合使用轻量潜变量标记器、原生分辨率多模态扩散变换器、整流流匹配、强化学习对齐和对抗感知引导的少步蒸馏。

03
差异

它不是只缩小主干网络，而是同时重做标记化、分辨率打包、网络结构和计算内核，并提供基础、对齐和高速模型变体。

04
证据

论文报告标记化成本降低一个数量级以上、端到端训练吞吐提升约二点五倍，并给出四步模型在一千零二十四平方分辨率下的生成和编辑延迟。

摘要

论文介绍了麦奇流，这是一个面向文本生图和指令式图像编辑的紧凑型四十亿参数级生成系统，由轻量高保真潜变量标记器和采用整流流匹配训练的原生分辨率多模态扩散变换器共同构成。该系统结合扩散式潜变量编码解码、原生分辨率打包、强化学习对齐和少步蒸馏，在保持生成与编辑效果的同时，将训练吞吐提高约二点五倍，并在单张英伟达加速卡上分别以零点五九秒和一点零二秒完成一千零二十四平方分辨率的生成与编辑。

为什么值得看 这项工作直接触及可交互世界模型的训练、长程推理和部署瓶颈：它用长程教师蒸馏与长程自回归对齐缓解误差累积，并把视频生成模型压到单张桌面级显卡上实时闭环运行，适合关注具身智能、游戏代理和可控视频生成的研究者。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 187）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

动作条件视频世界模型在长时程自回归交互中会受到分布偏移、误差累积和推理成本限制。

02
方法

系统结合多源数据采集、十四项确定性质量检查、视觉语言模型评估、双向教师到因果学生的蒸馏，以及长程强制对齐。

03
差异

它把长程教师监督、原始键盘控制、角色外观记忆和低比特流式推理放进同一套世界模型管线。

04
证据

在世界漫游基准和扩展交互轨迹上，作者报告了有竞争力的可控性与长时程演化一致性，并在单张桌面级显卡上达到每秒最高十六帧、动作到首帧一点二秒和约十九吉比特峰值显存。

摘要

我们提出阿博特世界零号，这是一个面向实时、长时程闭环交互的动作条件视频世界模型，并通过涵盖大型商业游戏、仿真引擎和互联网视频的多源数据基础设施学习可控世界动力学。系统使用世界探索器进行训练反馈引导的数据采集，通过教师强制和常微分方程蒸馏将双向动作条件教师模型逐步蒸馏为因果学生模型，并以长程强制使学生的长程自回归轨迹与扩展时域教师对齐，从而减轻分布偏移和自回归漂移；在单张英伟达高端桌面显卡上，优化后的低比特配置可生成每秒最高十六帧的七百二十像素视频，动作到首帧延迟为一点二秒，峰值显存约十九吉比特。

Yiyang Cai, Nan Chen, Rongchang Xie, Junwen Pan, Chunyang Jiang, Cheng Chen et al.
high · 2026-07-20

为什么值得看 这项工作直接针对主体驱动视频生成中的多模态条件融合：它在保留文本编码器可控性的同时，把多模态大语言模型提取的参考关系注入自注意力，并用模态与参考嵌入区分不同来源的标记。对需要同时保持人物或物体外观、交互关系和抽象标识物语义的个性化视频系统，这提供了避免昂贵重新对齐的一条实现路径。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 53）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有主体驱动视频方法难以同时维持主体保真度和人与物体之间的准确交互，且不能充分理解文字识别图或多视角等主体内参考之间的潜在对应关系。

02
方法

框架在自注意力中加入全局多模态引导，并使用模态与参考嵌入关联多模态大语言模型特征、变分自编码器标记和参考图像标记。

03
差异

方法统一处理主体间与主体内参考输入，并在引入多模态大语言模型知识时不改变文本编码器的可控性，也不需要昂贵的重新对齐。

04
证据

摘要称，大量实验在多种以人和物体为中心的视频个性化任务上验证了其领先性能。

摘要

以人和物体为中心的视频个性化是主体驱动视频生成中的核心任务，但现有方法难以同时保持高主体保真度和人与多样物体之间准确的交互模式，尤其是在物体是标识等抽象概念时。为解决主体间和主体内参考输入的共同问题，本文提出统一的视频个性化框架：通过自注意力中的全局多模态引导，将多模态大语言模型的语义特征更好地对齐到变分自编码器标记，并通过模态与参考嵌入区分多模态大语言模型特征、变分自编码器标记以及主体内参考图像标记；实验表明，该方法在多种任务上取得了领先性能。

Text Template Tokens Are Implicit Semantic Registers in Diffusion Transformers

分类方向模型与训练方法 / 架构设计主题diffusion / generative modeling
Maohua Li, Qirui Li, Yanke Zhou, Yiduo Li, Zhaosheng Chi, Chao Xu et al.
high · 2026-07-21

为什么值得看 这项工作揭示了扩散变换器中语义维护并不主要依赖输入端的提示词令牌：结构模板令牌会在去噪过程中充当隐式语义寄存器，因果地维持对象身份。对希望解释或加速大规模图像扩散模型的研究者而言，这一发现带来可操作的头部剪枝规则，在生成评测仅下降一点四分的情况下减少百分之二十的注意力浮点运算。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 68）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

研究文本到图像扩散变换器在去噪时如何分配提示词语义并维持对象身份。

02
方法

方法结合注意力分解，并对令牌跨度、注意力头和网络层实施定向因果干预。

03
差异

分析将提示词内容令牌与结构模板令牌分开，并追踪语义经图像潜变量回流到模板令牌的路径。

04
证据

作者报告剪除最关注提示词令牌的注意力头可减少百分之二十的注意力浮点运算，生成评测仅下降一点四分。

摘要

文本到图像扩散变换器共同处理文本令牌和图像令牌，但其去噪过程中的内部计算仍不清楚。本文提出一种结合注意力分解与跨令牌跨度、注意力头和层进行定向干预的因果可解释性方法，发现结构模板令牌虽然在编码器输出中几乎不包含提示词特定信息，却会成为图像到文本注意力的主要汇聚点，并因果地维持扩散变换器中的对象身份；其身份来自图像潜变量先接收提示词语义、再将语义读回模板令牌的间接过程。基于此，作者设计了无需训练的剪枝规则：最关注提示词令牌的注意力头可以移除，减少百分之二十的注意力浮点运算，而生成评测仅下降一点四分；研究还按层和注意力头区分了语义路由与视觉合成，以及从身份形成到传播和细化的生成计算过程。

AlayaWorld: Interactive Long-Horizon World Modeling -- Full Technical Report

分类方向模型与训练方法 / 架构设计主题diffusion / generative modeling
AlayaWorld Team, Kaipeng Zhang, Chuanhao Li, Yifan Zhan, Yongtao Ge, Yuanyang Yin et al.
high · 2026-07-20

为什么值得看 这项工作把视频扩散模型推进到可交互、长时域的世界建模：它同时处理相机轨迹、可切换文本提示、空间记忆和历史漂移，并将每个片段的采样步数从约三十步压到四步；对研究可探索环境生成、长时一致性和实时推理的读者尤其有价值。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 48）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

交互式视频世界模型需要同时维持交互响应、持久的时空一致性、稳定的长时域生成和高效推理。

02
方法

模型以一百五十亿参数的视频扩散变换器自回归生成短潜变量片段，并使用持久帧、压缩历史、几何对齐空间记忆和近期帧作为有界上下文。

03
差异

训练阶段加入模型自身滚动生成的受扰历史与预测残差，并用结合三类蒸馏方法的离散自回归蒸馏减少采样步骤。

04
证据

模型以每秒二十四帧和五百四十或七百二十像素分辨率生成视频，在长时域生成基准上取得最佳性能。

摘要

不同于依赖资产制作、动画、物理和编程等高成本流程的传统电子游戏开发，视频世界模型可以根据用户输入即时生成可交互环境，从文本、图像或视频创建定制化、可探索且持续演化的虚拟世界。我们提出阿拉雅世界，一个交互式长时域视频世界模型，以每秒二十四帧、五百四十或七百二十像素分辨率生成视频；它基于一百五十亿参数的视频扩散变换器，在相机轨迹和可切换文本提示的条件下自回归生成短潜变量片段，并结合持久汇聚帧、压缩时间历史、几何对齐空间记忆和近期帧条件构成有界视觉上下文。为减少长期漂移，模型使用自身滚动生成收集的受扰历史和预测残差进行训练；同时，离散自回归蒸馏结合分布匹配蒸馏、自强制加和一致性蒸馏，将每个片段的推理从约三十个采样步减少到四步。在长时域生成基准上，阿拉雅世界取得最佳性能。

Stale but Stable: Staleness-Adaptive Trust Regions for Stabilizing Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning

分类方向推理、智能体与后训练 / 后训练与对齐主题reinforcement learning
Junyao Yang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Ruhan Wang, Xiangxin Zhou et al.
high · 2026-07-21

为什么值得看 这项工作直接针对异步强化学习中的策略滞后与推理延迟，指出普通概率比率裁剪只约束采样到的更新，难以控制高滞后样本。其按滞后程度收缩概率比率区间，在保留普通令牌更新行为的同时压制失配尾部；在基于三百亿参数混合专家模型的异步实验中，长滞后条件下的艾梅二零二四平均八次采样得分达到三十四点七九，为大规模异步强化学习的稳定训练提供了可操作的信赖域机制。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 30）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

异步强化学习中的推理策略与训练策略不一致，且普通近端策略优化裁剪不能完整约束高陈旧性更新。

02
方法

方法用脱离梯度的采样对数比率估计陈旧性，并通过陈旧性核缩放收缩更新方向对应的概率比率区间端点。

03
差异

它保留普通令牌的基线裁剪行为，只对新识别出的高失配外侧区域施加更保守的约束。

04
证据

作者证明了局部区间包含性和相对于近端策略优化的逐点保守性，并在解耦异步训练中报告了不同滞后下的艾梅二零二四结果。

摘要

异步强化学习通过将轨迹生成与优化解耦来提高吞吐量，但策略滞后、引擎延迟和混合专家路由会共同造成不可避免的陈旧性。本文提出陈旧性自适应信赖域方法，使用脱离梯度的采样对数比率作为陈旧性代理，在每个批次中通过基于陈旧性的核缩放识别高失配尾部，并只收缩名义概率比率区间中由更新方向选定的端点；理论上证明了区间包含性和相对于近端策略优化的逐点保守性。基于解耦异步强化学习的实验表明，该方法结合路由重放能够在不同滞后条件下稳定训练，并在长滞后条件下取得艾梅二零二四平均八次采样三十四点七九的得分。

TimeLens2: Generalist Video Temporal Grounding with Multimodal LLMs

分类方向推理、智能体与后训练 / 后训练与对齐主题reinforcement learning
Yuhan Zhu, Changlian Ma, Xiangyu Zeng, Xinhao Li, Zhiqiu Zhang, Songze Li et al.
high · 2026-07-19

为什么值得看 这项工作把视频时间证据建模为可变数量的区间集合，并用无需片段匹配的稠密奖励直接优化多跨度定位；这对训练视频多模态大模型尤其有用，因为二十亿参数模型据称已在七个基准上超过同规模基线，并较其骨干模型提升最高十八点一个平均交并比点。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 160）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有训练方法难以处理长视频中的可变数量、多跨度时间证据，并且单次标注和片段匹配奖励都不稳健。

02
方法

方法使用九万三千条由候选生成、独立定位、跨智能体共识、语义核验和边界细化得到的多跨度监督，并联合时间瓦瑟斯坦奖励与时间交并比奖励进行优化。

03
差异

时间瓦瑟斯坦奖励在合并后的区间支撑集上计算一维距离，因此无需预测片段之间的一一匹配，并能处理不同区间数量和等价碎片化。

04
证据

二十亿参数版本在七个基准上超过同规模基线，四十亿和八十亿参数版本超过开源大模型，且相较骨干模型分别提升十四点二、十三点零和十八点一分平均交并比。

摘要

视频多模态大语言模型能够描述视频中发生的事情，却很少能指出证据出现的时间。本文研究通用视频时间定位：单个模型需要在不同视频长度、领域、查询形式和视角下，预测数量可变的证据区间集合。时间透镜二在监督和优化过程中始终将时间证据视为区间集合，并通过由字幕生成候选、独立定位、跨智能体共识、语义核验和边界细化构建多跨度监督；其时间瓦瑟斯坦奖励计算合并区间支撑集上均匀分布之间精确的一维一阶瓦瑟斯坦距离，在区间数量不等或碎片化等价时提供无需匹配的稠密反馈，同时以时间交并比补充精确重叠反馈。在七个基准上，二十亿参数版本超过所有同规模基线；四十亿和八十亿参数版本取得各模型规模中的最高表现，并超过参数量最高三千九百七十亿的开源模型。三个版本相较各自的千问三视觉语言骨干模型，平均交并比分别提升十四点二、十三点零和十八点一分。

为什么值得看 这项工作把可验证结果奖励下的强化学习扩展到连续潜在推理，针对潜在轨迹缺乏逐步似然和自适应停止接口这两个关键障碍，可能让推理模型在固定思考预算下用更短的连续向量轨迹获得测试时扩展能力。它尤其适合关注隐式推理、推理效率和结果奖励后训练的研究者。

方法解读

文本到图像扩散变换器共同处理文本令牌和图像令牌，但其去噪过程中的内部计算仍不清楚。本文提出一种结合注意力分解与跨令牌跨度、注意力头和层进行定向干预的因果可解释性方法，发现结构模板令牌虽然在编码器输出中几乎不包含提示词特定信息，却会成为图像到文本注意力的主要汇聚点，并因果地维持扩散变换器中的对象身份；其身份来自图像潜变量先接收提示词语义、再将语义读回模板令牌的间接过程。基于此，作者设计了无需训练的剪枝规则：最关注提示词令牌的注意力头可以移除，减少百分之二十的注意力浮点运算，而生成评测仅下降一点四分；研究还按层和注意力头区分了语义路由与视觉合成，以及从身份形成到传播和细化的生成计算过程。

Mage-Flow: An Efficient Native-Resolution Foundation Model for Image Generation and Editing

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
Xinjie Zhang, Peng Zhang, Shicheng Zheng, Jinghao Guo, Zhaoyang Jia, Yifei Shen et al.
high · 2026-07-21

Why it matters This work targets the practical bottlenecks of high-resolution diffusion systems rather than only scaling model capacity: tokenizer, native-resolution backbone, distillation, and CUDA execution are co-designed to cut tokenization cost, raise end-to-end training throughput by about 2.5×, and enable four-step interactive generation and editing on one A100. It is especially relevant to researchers studying efficient diffusion training, low-memory deployment, and fast image editing.

Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 57)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Large visual generators are expensive to train, fine-tune, and deploy, while high-resolution generation and editing remain latency-intensive.

02
Method

The system combines a one-step diffusion-style VAE with anchor-latent regularization, a native-resolution multimodal diffusion transformer trained by rectified flow matching, RL alignment, and adversarially guided few-step distillation.

03
Difference

Instead of reducing only the backbone size, it co-designs tokenization, resolution packing, model variants, and fused CUDA kernels across the full stack.

04
Evidence

The paper reports more than an order-of-magnitude lower tokenization cost, about 2.5× higher end-to-end training throughput, and 0.59-second generation plus 1.02-second editing at 1024² on a single A100 for the Turbo variants.

Abstract

Large-scale visual generators are increasingly capable but costly to train, fine-tune, and deploy. We introduce Mage-Flow, a compact 4B-scale generative stack for efficient text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing. The stack is built from two co-designed components: Mage-VAE, a lightweight high-fidelity latent tokenizer, and a Native-Resolution Multimodal Diffusion Transformer trained with rectified flow matching. Mage-VAE uses one-step diffusion-style encoding and decoding with anchor-latent regularization, preserving the reconstruction quality of strong public VAEs while reducing tokenization cost by more than an order of magnitude. Together with native-resolution packing and stack-level CUDA kernel fusion, the stack supports flexible-resolution training and improves end-to-end training throughput by about $2.5\times$. Built on this foundation, we develop a complete model family with Base, RL-aligned, and Turbo variants for both generation and editing. Diffusion-NFT improves prompt following, text rendering, aesthetic quality, and editing fidelity, while few-step distillation with adversarial perceptual guidance produces 4-step Turbo models for low-latency inference. Despite its compact scale, Mage-Flow and Mage-Flow-Edit achieves competitive performance across standard generation and editing benchmarks. More importantly, the Turbo variants make high-resolution generation and editing practical for interactive use: at $1024^2$ resolution on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, Mage-Flow-Turbo generates an image in 0.59s, and Mage-Flow-Edit-Turbo edits an image in 1.02s, while maintaining a small memory footprint. These results show that careful tokenizer--backbone--system co-design can deliver strong high-resolution generation and editing within an efficient 4B model family.

ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
Fan Jiang, Zhaoxu Sun, Mengchao Wang, Ziyu Zhu, Chiyu Wang, Yunpeng Zhang et al.
high · 2026-07-21

Why it matters This paper targets a core bottleneck for interactive world models: keeping long closed-loop rollouts coherent while meeting desktop-GPU latency and memory limits. Long-horizon teacher alignment, action-conditioned distillation, and the reported 720p streaming setup make it relevant to embodied agents, game agents, and controllable video generation researchers.

Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 187)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Action-conditioned video world models suffer from distribution shift, autoregressive drift, and expensive inference during long interactive rollouts.

02
Method

The system combines multi-source collection, deterministic and VLM quality checks, bidirectional-teacher-to-causal-student distillation, and LongForcing alignment against an extended-horizon teacher.

03
Difference

It unifies long-horizon supervision, raw keyboard control, reference-character memory, and low-bit streaming inference in one world-model pipeline.

04
Evidence

The paper reports competitive controllability and coherent evolution on WorldRoamBench and extended rollouts, with up to 16 FPS at 720p, 1.2-second action-to-first-frame latency, and about 19 GiB peak VRAM on one RTX 5090.

Abstract

We present ABot-World-0, an action-conditioned video world model for real-time, long-horizon closed-loop interaction, supported by a multi-source data infrastructure spanning AAA games, simulation engines, and internet videos to learn controllable world dynamics. WorldExplorer performs agent-driven collection guided by training feedback, while a unified pipeline applies 14 deterministic quality checks, VLM-based assessment, and synchronized action and text annotation. We progressively distill a bidirectional action-conditioned teacher into a causal student through teacher forcing and ODE distillation, and introduce LongForcing to align long student self-rollouts with an extended-horizon teacher, mitigating accumulated distribution shift and autoregressive drift. Raw keyboard actions provide a unified control interface for scene roaming and third-person character interaction, while reference-character memory provides persistent appearance cues for identity consistency during third-person rollouts. For deployment, we co-design a streaming inference stack with a lightweight VAE decoder, efficient attention, memory-aware scheduling, and low-bit DiT inference. Across optimized low-bit configurations, ABot-World-0 streams 720P video at up to 16 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 desktop GPU, with 1.2s action-to-first-frame latency and approximately 19GiB peak VRAM. Experiments on WorldRoamBench and extended interactive rollouts demonstrate competitive controllability and coherent long-horizon world evolution.

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
Yiyang Cai, Nan Chen, Rongchang Xie, Junwen Pan, Chunyang Jiang, Cheng Chen et al.
high · 2026-07-20

Why it matters This work targets a concrete multimodal-conditioning bottleneck in subject-driven video generation: injecting reference-level relations from a multimodal language model while preserving text-encoder controllability and avoiding costly re-alignment. It is relevant to systems that must preserve identity, human–object interactions, and abstract object semantics such as logos across personalized videos.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 53)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing subject-driven video methods struggle to preserve subject fidelity and accurate human–object interactions, while missing latent correspondences in intra-subject references such as OCR maps and multi-view inputs.

02
Method

HOMIE adds global multimodal guidance inside self-attention and uses modality-reference embeddings to associate multimodal-language-model features, VAE tokens, and intra-subject reference image tokens.

Abstract

Human-object centric video personalization (HOCVP) is a core task within subject-driven video generation. However, existing methods suffer from two key limitations. First, most approaches focusing on inter-subject personalization still struggle to strike a balance between high subject fidelity and accurate interaction patterns between humans and diverse objects, especially when objects represent abstract concepts such as logos. Second, while intra-subject references (e.g., OCR maps, multi-view inputs) are expected to enhance subject fidelity, most existing works lack mechanisms to understand such latent correspondence. To address both challenges, we propose HOMIE, an HOCVP framework that tackles both inter- and intra-subject input settings in a unified manner. Compared to previous approaches, HOMIE proposes a better MLLM integration strategy to extract knowledge of reference-level relationships without compromising the controllability of text encoders or incurring costly re-alignment. Specifically, we introduce global multimodal guidance within self-attention to better align MLLM-derived semantic features with VAE tokens. Furthermore, we propose modality-reference embedding to differentiate tokens from MLLM features and VAE tokens and associate intra-subject reference image tokens. Extensive experiments validate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across various HOCVP tasks. Project Page: https://yiyangcai.github.io/homie-page.github.io/

Text Template Tokens Are Implicit Semantic Registers in Diffusion Transformers

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
Maohua Li, Qirui Li, Yanke Zhou, Yiduo Li, Zhaosheng Chi, Chao Xu et al.
high · 2026-07-21

Why it matters This work shows that semantic maintenance in diffusion transformers need not rely on the tokens that carry semantics at the input: structural template tokens become implicit semantic registers that causally preserve object identity during denoising. For researchers explaining or accelerating large image diffusion models, it also yields a usable training-free pruning rule that removes 20% of attention FLOPs with a 1.4-point GenEval drop.

Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 68)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper studies how text-to-image diffusion transformers route prompt semantics and preserve object identity during denoising.

02
Method

It combines attention decomposition with targeted causal interventions over token spans, heads, and layers.

03
Difference

The analysis separates prompt-content tokens from structural template tokens and traces semantics as they move through image latents back into the template tokens.

04
Evidence

The authors report that pruning heads attending most strongly to prompt tokens cuts attention FLOPs by 20% while reducing GenEval by only 1.4 points.

Abstract

Text-to-image diffusion transformers (DiTs) jointly process text and image tokens, yet their internal computation during denoising remains poorly understood. We introduce a causal interpretability framework for modern large-scale DiTs that combines attention decomposition with targeted interventions across token spans, heads, and layers. Using it to separate prompt-content tokens from structural template tokens, we find that the structural tokens carry little prompt-specific information at the encoder output. Yet surprisingly, they emerge as dominant image-to-text attention sinks and causally maintain object identity inside the DiT, acting as implicit semantic registers. We show that they acquire this identity indirectly, with prompt semantics first injected into the image latents and then read back into the template tokens rather than transferred directly from the prompt tokens. Inspired by the above findings, we design a training-free pruning rule for DiTs. Heads that attend most strongly to prompt tokens are dispensable, and pruning them removes $20\%$ of attention FLOPs with only a $1.4$-point drop on GenEval. We further reveal how generative computation in DiTs is organized across heads and depth, separating semantic routing from visual synthesis and progressing from identity formation to propagation and refinement. Our work not only reveals that the tokens encoding semantics at input need not be those that maintain it during generation, but also provides a causal view of internal mechanisms in DiTs.

AlayaWorld: Interactive Long-Horizon World Modeling -- Full Technical Report

CategoryAreaModels and Training Methods / Architecture DesignTopicdiffusion / generative modeling
AlayaWorld Team, Kaipeng Zhang, Chuanhao Li, Yifan Zhan, Yongtao Ge, Yuanyang Yin et al.
high · 2026-07-20

Why it matters This work moves video diffusion toward interactive, long-horizon world modeling by coupling camera-conditioned generation, switchable language control, spatial memory, and drift correction; it also cuts sampling from about 30 steps to four per chunk, making it relevant to researchers targeting persistent environments and faster rollout.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 48)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Interactive video world models must maintain interaction, persistent spatiotemporal consistency, stable long-horizon generation, and efficient response at once.

02
Method

A 15B video diffusion transformer autoregressively generates short latent chunks using a persistent sink frame, compressed history, geometry-aligned spatial memory, and recent-frame conditioning.

03

The training process uses corrupted histories and prediction residuals from the model's own roll-outs, while discrete autoregressive distillation combines distribution matching, self-forcing++, and consistency distillation.

Abstract

Unlike conventional video game development, which relies on labor-intensive pipelines for asset production, animation, physics, and programming, video world models generate interactive environments from user inputs instantly. It enable us to create customized, explorable, and continuously evolving virtual world from text, an image, or video. Realizing this vision requires four tightly coupled capabilities: interaction, persistent spatiotemporal consistency, stable long-horizon generation, and efficient response. We present AlayaWorld, an interactive long-horizon video world model that generates 24-fps video at 540p and 720p. Built on a 15B video diffusion transformer, AlayaWorld generates short latent chunks autoregressively under camera trajectories and switchable text prompts. Its bounded visual context combines a persistent sink frame, compressed temporal history, geometry-aligned spatial memory, and recent-frame conditioning. To reduce long-term drift, the model is trained with corrupted histories and prediction residuals collected from its own roll-outs. We further introduce a discrete autoregressive distillation formulation that combines distribution-matching distillation, self-forcing++, and consistency distillation, reducing inference from approximately 30 sampling steps to four steps per chunk. On iWorld-Bench, AlayaWorld achieves the best performance over long-horizon generation. Conceived as a full-stack, open-source, and long-term project, AlayaWorld is intended to provide an extensible foundation for future research on interactive video world models.

Stale but Stable: Staleness-Adaptive Trust Regions for Stabilizing Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning

CategoryAreaReasoning, Agents, and Post-Training / Post-Training and AlignmentTopicreinforcement learning
Junyao Yang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Ruhan Wang, Xiangxin Zhou et al.
high · 2026-07-21

Why it matters This paper targets a concrete failure mode in asynchronous RL: policy lag and inference delay make ordinary PPO clipping too weak for high-staleness samples because it constrains sampled updates rather than the full mismatch. By shrinking trust-region endpoints according to a detached log-ratio proxy, SAT leaves ordinary-token behavior mostly unchanged while tightening the mismatch tail; on an asynchronous Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base setup, it reports AIME24 avg@8 of 34.79 at lag 8, offering a practical stabilization mechanism for large-scale decoupled RL.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 30)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Asynchronous RL creates training-inference mismatch, while PPO clipping does not fully control updates from highly stale rollouts.

02
Method

SAT estimates staleness with a detached sampled log-ratio, identifies high-mismatch tails through staleness-based kernel scaling, and contracts the sign-selected endpoint of the PPO interval.

03
Difference

The rule preserves baseline clipping for ordinary tokens and adds stronger constraints only to newly intercepted outward bands.

04
Evidence

The paper proves local interval containment and pointwise pessimism relative to PPO, then reports AIME24 avg@8 results across lag 1 and lag 8 in a decoupled asynchronous setup.

Abstract

Asynchronous reinforcement learning improves throughput by decoupling rollout generation from optimization, but staleness is an inevitable byproduct compounded by policy lag, engine delays, and mixture-of-experts routing. From a trust-region perspective, this mismatch is critical: training-inference divergence governs approximation error in finite-horizon bounds, whereas PPO clipping only gates sampled outward updates, acting as a sampled surrogate rather than a full-policy constraint. As a result, high-staleness updates remain weakly controlled in the asynchronous regime where stale rollouts matter most. We introduce the Staleness-Adaptive Trust Region (SAT), which uses the detached sampled log-ratio as a practical staleness proxy, identifies high-mismatch tails within each batch via staleness-based kernel scaling, and contracts only the sign-selected endpoint of the nominal PPO interval. This preserves baseline behavior on ordinary tokens while enforcing more conservative updates on newly intercepted outward bands. We prove local interval containment and pointwise pessimism relative to PPO, showing how the adaptive rule reshapes update geometry under heterogeneous staleness. We evaluate SAT in a decoupled asynchronous RL setup built on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, using SGLang as the inference engine and Megatron for training. In this setting, SAT-GSPO w/ R3 achieves the best observed AIME24 avg@8, reaching 35.83 at lag 1 and 34.79 at lag 8, while SAT-GSPO reaches 34.17 at lag 1. Adaptive clipping and routing replay act as complementary stabilizers targeting mismatch tails and routing inconsistency, respectively. Overall, aligning clip intervals with staleness heterogeneity effectively stabilizes asynchronous RL.

Code
Method brief
01
Problem

02
Method

The system builds 93K multi-span examples through proposal generation, independent localization, cross-agent consensus, semantic verification, and boundary refinement, then optimizes temporal Wasserstein and temporal IoU rewards.

Abstract

Video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can describe what happens in a video, but rarely identify when the supporting evidence occurs. We study generalist video temporal grounding, in which one model predicts a variable-cardinality set of evidence intervals across video lengths, domains, query forms, and viewpoints. Existing training strategies are misaligned with this set-valued task: long-video labels often rely on brittle one-pass annotation, while reinforcement-learning rewards either fail to distinguish non-overlapping predictions or require fragile segment matching. TimeLens2 treats temporal evidence as an interval set throughout supervision and optimization. TimeLens2-93K constructs reliable multi-span supervision through caption-derived proposals, independent localization, cross-agent consensus, semantic verification, and boundary refinement. Our temporal Wasserstein reward computes exact one-dimensional \(W_1\) between uniform distributions over merged interval supports, providing dense, matching-free feedback under unequal cardinalities and equivalent fragmentation; temporal IoU complements it with precise-overlap feedback. Across seven benchmarks, TimeLens2-2B outperforms all size-matched baselines on every benchmark, while the 4B and 8B variants achieve state-of-the-art performance, surpassing open-source models with up to 397B parameters. The 2B, 4B, and 8B variants improve over their Qwen3-VL backbones by 14.2, 13.0, and 18.1 mIoU points, respectively.

In this paper, we introduce DocOps, a deterministically verifiable evaluation framework underpinned by a hierarchical taxonomy that deconstructs document operations inspired by real-world practices into atomic dimensions and escalating workflow complexities. Based on DocOps, we systematically evaluate representative closed- and open-source models across various agentic harnesses, revealing that even the most advanced frontier configurations still exhibit profound limitations when handling highly coupled, long-range tasks. Furthermore, a fine-grained analysis of existing agents' manipulation behaviors uncovers 3 key failure modes: long-term state tracking collapse, shallow semantic verification, and destructive editing of structural metadata. Ultimately, our work exposes the capability boundaries of agents in maintaining global document consistency, shedding light on the future design of robust, non-destructive agents for complex digital ecosystems.

分类方向编译器、内核与硬件 / GPU/加速器内核主题accelerator / edge inference
Xinjie Zhang, Peng Zhang, Shicheng Zheng, Jinghao Guo, Zhaoyang Jia, Yifei Shen et al.
medium · 2026-07-21

为什么值得看 这项工作把视觉生成模型、潜空间分词器与加速卡内核融合一起优化：分词成本降低一个数量级以上，端到端训练吞吐提升约二点五倍，并在单张英伟达加速卡上实现高分辨率低延迟生成和编辑，适合关注视觉模型训练与推理系统效率的研究者。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 57）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

大规模视觉生成模型的训练、微调和部署成本较高，尤其是潜空间标记化与高分辨率处理环节。

02
方法

系统采用带锚点潜变量正则的一步扩散式编码解码器，并结合原生分辨率多模态扩散变换器、整流流匹配和少步蒸馏。

03
差异

它不是只压缩主干模型，而是联合设计分词器、生成主干和加速卡执行栈，并提供基础、强化学习对齐和快速推理版本。

04
证据

摘要称分词成本降低超过一个数量级、端到端训练吞吐提升约二点五倍，快速版本在一千零二十四乘一千零二十四分辨率下生成和编辑分别耗时零点五九秒与一点零二秒。

摘要

本文介绍了一个紧凑的四十亿参数级视觉生成系统，由轻量高保真潜空间分词器和采用整流流匹配训练的原生分辨率多模态扩散变换器共同组成。通过原生分辨率打包与加速卡内核融合，系统支持灵活分辨率训练并提升端到端训练吞吐；其少步蒸馏模型可在单张英伟达加速卡上以较低延迟完成高分辨率图像生成与编辑，同时保持较小的显存占用。

为什么值得看 这项工作把长时闭环世界模型的部署问题具体化为单张桌面级图形处理器上的流式推理：通过轻量解码器、高效注意力、显存感知调度和低比特扩散变换器推理，实现七百二十像素视频最高每秒十六帧、动作到首帧一点二秒和约十九吉比显存峰值；对需要低成本交互式视频生成的推理系统研究者尤其有参考价值。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 187）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

系统要在实时交互中维持动作可控性、长时世界演化和可接受的单卡推理成本。

02
方法

方法结合智能体驱动的数据采集、双向教师到因果学生的蒸馏、长时蒸馏以及面向部署的流式推理优化。

03
差异

长时蒸馏让学生自回滚与延长视野的教师对齐，并以统一键盘动作和参考角色记忆支持不同交互场景。

04
证据

在世界漫游基准和扩展交互回滚实验中，系统声称具备有竞争力的可控性和连贯的长时世界演化，并报告单卡流式性能。

摘要

本文介绍一种动作条件视频世界模型及其数据基础设施，覆盖大型商业游戏、仿真引擎和互联网视频，并通过智能体驱动的数据采集、确定性质量检查、视觉语言模型评估以及同步动作和文本标注学习可控的世界动力学。系统将双向动作条件教师模型逐步蒸馏为因果学生模型，并用长时蒸馏减轻自回归漂移；配合流式推理栈、轻量变分自编码器解码器、高效注意力、显存感知调度和低比特扩散变换器推理，在单张英伟达锐龙五零九零桌面级图形处理器上以最高每秒十六帧流式生成七百二十像素视频，动作到首帧延迟一点二秒，显存峰值约十九吉比。

为什么值得看 这项工作直接说明苹果硅片上的神经加速器可以改变本地大模型推理的性能上限：通过手写张量核心内核，提示词处理吞吐相对现有运行时最高提升六点四倍，尤其适合矩阵乘法占主导的混合专家模型；而解码阶段仍使用专用内核处理内存带宽瓶颈。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

苹果硅片上的大语言模型运行时需要同时处理计算密集型预填充和内存密集型解码。

02
方法

基础运行时使用原生金属实现，并加入面向神经加速器的稠密矩阵乘法、混合专家矩阵乘法和闪存注意力内核。

03
差异

它只把预填充中的计算密集型矩阵乘法迁移到片上神经加速器，而不是用同一套路径覆盖整个推理过程。

04
证据

在覆盖四个模型系列、参数量从不足十亿到三百五十亿的十五种配置上，论文报告了相对两个基线的提示词处理和解码吞吐优势。

摘要

苹果第五代芯片重新设计了图形处理器架构，使每个核心都配备专用神经加速器，并通过金属四张量接口提供片上矩阵单元。本文介绍原生金属推理运行时基础运行时，通过手写稠密与混合专家矩阵乘法内核以及闪存注意力预填充内核，将计算密集型矩阵乘法交给神经加速器，同时保留面向内存密集型解码的专用内核；在苹果第五代专业芯片上的十五种模型配置中，提示词处理吞吐最高达到开源轻量运行时的六点四倍和机器学习运行时的三点九倍，解码吞吐最高分别达到一点七五倍和一点三三倍。

为什么值得看 这项工作把原本依赖随机采样和非线性距离计算的概率检索改造成一次矩阵向量乘法可执行的确定性流程，使概率语义不确定性能够部署到存内计算交叉阵列上；六个视频、图像和音频检索基准上，第一名召回率相对确定性基线最高提升百分之十点三，并在器件非理想性仿真下保持稳健。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

概率跨模态检索需要采样与非线性距离计算，而传统交叉阵列只支持确定性的单步矩阵向量乘法。

02
方法

方法用低阶多项式基表示高斯嵌入，并用可学习的阶数双线性核计算分布相似度。

03
差异

它在保留分布信息的同时去除推理阶段的随机采样，使整个检索流程适配常规存内计算交叉阵列。

04
证据

六个检索基准显示第一名召回率相对确定性基线最高提升百分之十点三，并在器件非理想性仿真中达到稳健部署结果。

摘要

边缘设备上的跨模态检索可以利用概率嵌入表达语义不确定性，但依赖蒙特卡洛采样和非线性距离计算的现有方法难以运行在只支持确定性单步矩阵向量乘法的存内计算交叉阵列上。该方法用低阶多项式基表示高斯嵌入的各维，并通过可学习的阶数双线性核计算相似度，从而消除随机采样；在六个基准上相对确定性基线的第一名召回率最高提升百分之十点三，并在现实器件非理想性仿真中验证了部署稳健性。

为什么值得看 这项工作面向资源受限设备上的卷积神经网络推理，展示了如何通过列式压缩、可配置二维乘加阵列以及面向微架构的剪枝协同设计，把不规则稀疏性映射到现场可编程门阵列上；对关注边缘推理硬件、稀疏执行和能效权衡的研究者有参考价值。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

不规则非结构化稀疏性难以高效映射到现场可编程门阵列，而结构化稀疏性会牺牲灵活性和模型精度。

02
方法

系统采用可扩展二维乘加阵列、列式卷积核压缩、排序优化以及多阶段结构化剪枝与恢复算法。

03
差异

它将稀疏格式、剪枝策略和加速器微架构联合设计，而不是只在硬件或算法一侧处理稀疏性。

04
证据

在维基十六和残差网络十八上，结构化稀疏模式分别达到超过二点五万亿次每秒和一百零五十亿次每焦耳、超过一点一万亿次每秒和七十二十亿次每焦耳。

摘要

高效加速卷积神经网络在资源受限平台上仍面临稀疏模式不规则和硬件开销大的问题。本文提出一种基于现场可编程门阵列的可配置加速器，通过列式卷积核压缩、二维乘加阵列、排序优化以及多阶段结构化剪枝与恢复算法，在灵活稀疏性和硬件效率之间取得平衡；在低成本的超大规模现场可编程门阵列上，模型在保持较小精度下降的同时取得了较高的吞吐率和能效。

为什么值得看 这篇报告直接覆盖万亿参数混合专家模型在昇腾超级集群上的全参数后训练，给出从并行策略、计算通信编排到低层内核执行的系统优化路径；其报告的模型浮点运算利用率达到百分之三十四点二二，相比开源基线配方提升二点九三倍，对需要在非英伟达集群上推进大模型后训练的系统团队尤其有参考价值。

来源信号arXiv 收录Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 31）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

目标是解决昇腾集群上万亿参数混合专家模型全参数后训练中的内存、通信和内核效率问题。

02
方法

系统按模型级并行、计算通信编排和低层内核执行三个层次进行端到端优化，并配套运筹学持续预训练与监督微调数据流程。

03
差异

工作将非英伟达超级集群上的训练基础设施优化与求解器验证的领域数据管线结合，而不只调整模型或数据的一侧。

04
证据

报告称模型浮点运算利用率为百分之三十四点二二、相对开源基线提升二点九三倍，专用模型平均零样本第一候选准确率为百分之七十一点八一。

摘要

万亿参数规模混合专家模型的全参数后训练面临显存压力大、通信难以重叠以及内核执行低效等系统挑战。该报告以深度求索模型家族为负载，在昇腾超级集群上构建覆盖模型并行、计算通信编排和底层内核执行的分层优化系统，使模型浮点运算利用率达到百分之三十四点二二，并在保持训练稳定的同时达到开源基线配方的二点九三倍。基于这套基础设施，报告还构建了面向运筹学任务的持续预训练和监督微调流程，使用四类任务、三种问题表示的高质量数据训练专用模型，其零样本第一候选准确率平均达到百分之七十一点八一，并超过所比较的模型。

为什么值得看 奥丁把分布式点渲染训练的同步粒度从任务或迭代级降到原子基元级，直接缩短渲染器变快后由全局屏障造成的等待。它适合场景状态稀疏更新、视图依赖明显的训练系统；在八个图形处理器上平均提升吞吐一点评二二倍并隐藏百分之八十二的关键路径等待，在六十四个图形处理器的混合并行案例中相对格伦德尔最高提升一点评八九倍，且不修改渲染内核、优化器、训练预算或模型容量。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

点渲染训练中的视图依赖基元状态会让全局任务级和迭代级屏障成为主要等待来源。

02
方法

提前调度器利用稳定局部性和阶段顺序寻找低冲突重叠窗口，运行时在后续工作读取前验证基元是否已发布。

03
差异

系统按基元而不是整个任务或迭代进行同步，并根据梯度证据选择性容忍低影响的延迟读取。

04
证据

四个训练流程、十三个场景和八个图形处理器上的实验显示平均吞吐提升一点评二二倍并隐藏百分之八十二的关键路径等待。

摘要

基于点的神经渲染以显式、可训练的基元表示三维场景，但每个视图只读取和更新稀疏且随视图变化的可变场景状态，因此大规模分布式训练中的全局任务级或迭代级屏障可能使同步而非渲染成为关键路径。奥丁以基元级同步替代全局屏障，通过提前调度器寻找低冲突重叠窗口，并由运行时验证基元发布；它提供保持同步训练可见性的质量优先路径，以及仅允许小范围低影响延迟读取的吞吐优先路径，在四个点渲染训练流程和十三个非城市场景上平均提升吞吐一点评二二倍，同时保持重建质量。

Mage-Flow: An Efficient Native-Resolution Foundation Model for Image Generation and Editing

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Xinjie Zhang, Peng Zhang, Shicheng Zheng, Jinghao Guo, Zhaoyang Jia, Yifei Shen et al.
medium · 2026-07-21

Why it matters This work co-designs the visual generator, latent tokenizer, and GPU execution path: it claims more than an order-of-magnitude lower tokenization cost, about 2.5x higher end-to-end training throughput, and practical high-resolution generation and editing on one NVIDIA GPU. It is most useful to researchers optimizing training and inference stacks for image-generation models.

Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 57)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Large visual generators impose high training, fine-tuning, and deployment costs, including the cost of latent tokenization and high-resolution processing.

02
Method

The stack combines a one-step diffusion-style tokenizer with anchor-latent regularization, a native-resolution multimodal diffusion transformer trained by rectified flow matching, CUDA kernel fusion, and few-step distillation.

03
Difference

Rather than compressing only the backbone, it jointly designs the tokenizer, generator, and GPU execution stack and supplies base, RL-aligned, and turbo variants.

04
Evidence

The abstract reports over an order-of-magnitude lower tokenization cost, about 2.5x higher end-to-end training throughput, and 0.59-second generation and 1.02-second editing at 1024² resolution on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.

Abstract

Large-scale visual generators are increasingly capable but costly to train, fine-tune, and deploy. We introduce Mage-Flow, a compact 4B-scale generative stack for efficient text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing. The stack is built from two co-designed components: Mage-VAE, a lightweight high-fidelity latent tokenizer, and a Native-Resolution Multimodal Diffusion Transformer trained with rectified flow matching. Mage-VAE uses one-step diffusion-style encoding and decoding with anchor-latent regularization, preserving the reconstruction quality of strong public VAEs while reducing tokenization cost by more than an order of magnitude. Together with native-resolution packing and stack-level CUDA kernel fusion, the stack supports flexible-resolution training and improves end-to-end training throughput by about $2.5\times$. Built on this foundation, we develop a complete model family with Base, RL-aligned, and Turbo variants for both generation and editing. Diffusion-NFT improves prompt following, text rendering, aesthetic quality, and editing fidelity, while few-step distillation with adversarial perceptual guidance produces 4-step Turbo models for low-latency inference. Despite its compact scale, Mage-Flow and Mage-Flow-Edit achieves competitive performance across standard generation and editing benchmarks. More importantly, the Turbo variants make high-resolution generation and editing practical for interactive use: at $1024^2$ resolution on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, Mage-Flow-Turbo generates an image in 0.59s, and Mage-Flow-Edit-Turbo edits an image in 1.02s, while maintaining a small memory footprint. These results show that careful tokenizer--backbone--system co-design can deliver strong high-resolution generation and editing within an efficient 4B model family.

ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference

Why it matters This paper turns long-horizon interactive world-model deployment into a concrete single-GPU serving problem: a lightweight VAE decoder, efficient attention, memory-aware scheduling, and low-bit DiT inference reach up to 16 FPS at 720P, 1.2 s action-to-first-frame latency, and about 19 GiB peak VRAM on one RTX 5090. Source signalsarXiv indexedHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 187)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

The system must preserve controllability and coherent long-horizon evolution while serving interactive video at real-time-like rates on one GPU.

02
Method

It combines agent-driven data collection, bidirectional-teacher to causal-student distillation, LongForcing, and a deployment stack optimized for streaming inference.

03
Difference

LongForcing aligns student self-rollouts with an extended-horizon teacher, while unified keyboard actions and reference-character memory cover roaming and third-person interaction.

04
Evidence

Abstract

We present ABot-World-0, an action-conditioned video world model for real-time, long-horizon closed-loop interaction, supported by a multi-source data infrastructure spanning AAA games, simulation engines, and internet videos to learn controllable world dynamics. WorldExplorer performs agent-driven collection guided by training feedback, while a unified pipeline applies 14 deterministic quality checks, VLM-based assessment, and synchronized action and text annotation. We progressively distill a bidirectional action-conditioned teacher into a causal student through teacher forcing and ODE distillation, and introduce LongForcing to align long student self-rollouts with an extended-horizon teacher, mitigating accumulated distribution shift and autoregressive drift. Raw keyboard actions provide a unified control interface for scene roaming and third-person character interaction, while reference-character memory provides persistent appearance cues for identity consistency during third-person rollouts. For deployment, we co-design a streaming inference stack with a lightweight VAE decoder, efficient attention, memory-aware scheduling, and low-bit DiT inference. Across optimized low-bit configurations, ABot-World-0 streams 720P video at up to 16 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 desktop GPU, with 1.2s action-to-first-frame latency and approximately 19GiB peak VRAM. Experiments on WorldRoamBench and extended interactive rollouts demonstrate competitive controllability and coherent long-horizon world evolution.

BaseRT: Advancing Best-in-Class LLM Inference with Apple M5 Neural Accelerators

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Fabian Waschkowski, Prabod Rathnayaka, Lukas Wesemann
high · 2026-07-21

Why it matters This paper gives Apple Silicon inference engineers a concrete path to exploit M5's on-die neural accelerators: hand-written tensor kernels raise prompt-processing throughput by up to 6.4× over llama.cpp, with the largest gains on matrix-heavy mixture-of-experts models, while specialized kernels continue to handle memory-bound decode.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

LLM inference on Apple Silicon must handle compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode with different bottlenecks.

02
Method

BaseRT uses a native Metal runtime with hand-written dense GEMM, mixture-of-experts GEMM, and flash-attention prefill kernels targeting M5 Neural Accelerators.

03
Difference

04

Across fifteen configurations covering Qwen, Llama, and Gemma families from sub-1B to 35B parameters, the paper reports up to 6.4× prompt-processing and 1.75× decode speedups over llama.cpp.

Abstract

Apple's M5 generation introduces a redesigned GPU architecture in which every core carries a dedicated Neural Accelerator: on-die matrix units exposed through the Metal~4 tensor API. We show that BaseRT, our native Metal inference runtime for large language models on Apple Silicon, exploits these units to push inference throughput on Apple hardware substantially beyond both llama.cpp and MLX. Building on BaseRT's framework-free design, we add a family of hand-written Metal~4 tensor-core kernels (including dense and mixture-of-experts GEMM and flash-attention prefill kernels) that route the compute-bound matrix multiplications of inference through the M5 Neural Accelerators while leaving the memory-bound decode path on our existing specialised kernels. On an Apple M5 Pro, across fifteen model configurations spanning the Qwen3, Qwen3.5/3.6, Llama~3.2, and Gemma~4 families from sub-1B to 35B parameters, BaseRT delivers up to $6.4\times$ higher prompt-processing throughput than llama.cpp and $3.9\times$ higher than MLX, with the largest margins on the mixture-of-experts models where matrix multiplication dominates, while maintaining its lead on decode of up to $1.75\times$ over llama.cpp and $1.33\times$ over MLX. These results establish a new performance ceiling for on-device LLM inference and show that the M5's tensor cores are the decisive lever for prompt processing on Apple Silicon. BaseRT is publicly available at https://github.com/basecompute/baseRT.

PolySim: Deterministic Polynomial Surrogates for Cross-Modal Retrieval on CiM

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Xinzhao Li, Charles Power, Pengyu Ren, Jongun Won, Likai Pei, Yuting Hu et al.
high · 2026-07-22

Why it matters PolySim turns probabilistic cross-modal retrieval into a deterministic, single-matrix-vector-multiplication pipeline that can run on compute-in-memory crossbars, rather than requiring Monte Carlo sampling and nonlinear distance evaluation. Across six video, image, and audio benchmarks, it improves R@1 over deterministic baselines by up to 10.3% and remains robust under simulated device non-idealities.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Probabilistic retrieval methods require sampling and nonlinear distance computation that conventional crossbars cannot execute directly.

02
Method

The method represents each Gaussian embedding dimension with low-order polynomial bases and uses a learnable order-bilinear kernel for similarity.

03
Difference

It removes stochastic inference while retaining distributional information and reducing execution to a crossbar-compatible matrix-vector multiplication.

04
Evidence

Experiments on six retrieval benchmarks report up to a 10.3% R@1 gain over deterministic baselines, with CrossSim evaluation showing robustness to realistic device non-idealities.

Abstract

Cross-modal retrieval on edge devices benefits from probabilistic embeddings that capture semantic uncertainty, but deploying them on compute-in-memory (CiM) hardware remains an open problem. The core difficulty is a sampling gap: probabilistic methods such as PCME rely on Monte Carlo sampling and nonlinear distance evaluation at inference, which are fundamentally incompatible with CiM crossbar arrays that support only deterministic, single-step matrix-vector multiplication. Few existing probabilistic retrieval methods can be executed on a conventional crossbar. To bridge this gap, we propose PolySim, a framework that reformulates probabilistic retrieval into a fully deterministic pipeline. PolySim approximates each Gaussian embedding dimension using low-order polynomial bases and computes similarity via a learnable order-bilinear kernel, eliminating stochastic sampling while preserving distributional information. In experiments on six benchmarks spanning video, image, and audio retrieval, PolySim improves R@1 over deterministic baselines by up to 10.3\% and matches or exceeds PCME, while reducing inference to a single crossbar-compatible matrix-vector multiplication. CrossSim evaluation under realistic device non-idealities confirms robust deployment on conventional crossbar arrays. To the best of our knowledge, PolySim is the first method to enable probabilistic cross-modal retrieval on CiM hardware.

A Flexible Sparsity-Aware FPGA Accelerator with Column-Wise Compression for Efficient CNN Inference

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Amirhossein Zarei, Shervin Vakili
medium · 2026-07-21

Why it matters This work targets CNN inference on resource-constrained devices and shows how column-wise compression, a configurable 2D MAC array, and hardware-aware pruning can map irregular sparsity onto an FPGA with limited overhead. Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

02
Method

The accelerator combines a scalable 2D MAC array, column-wise kernel compression, ordering optimization, and multi-phase structured pruning and revival.

Abstract

Efficient acceleration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on resource-constrained platforms remains challenging due to the irregularity of sparsity patterns and the associated hardware overhead. While unstructured sparsity offers high model accuracy, it introduces significant inefficiencies in hardware mapping, whereas structured sparsity simplifies execution at the cost of reduced flexibility. This paper presents SparHiXcel-v2, a cost-effective and highly configurable FPGA-based CNN accelerator that achieves an improved balance between sparsity flexibility and hardware efficiency. The proposed architecture is built around a scalable two-dimensional MAC array and introduces a column-wise kernel compression technique that enables efficient handling of irregular sparsity patterns with minimal hardware overhead. To further enhance performance, we propose a hardware-algorithm co-design framework, including an ordering optimization scheme and a multi-phase structured pruning and revival algorithm tailored to the microarchitecture. Extensive evaluations on VGG16 and ResNet18 demonstrate that SparHiXcel-v2 achieves substantial improvements in processing throughput and energy efficiency through the proposed optimizations. In structured sparsity mode, the accelerator reaches over 2.5 TOPS and 210 GOP/s/W for VGG16, and over 1.1 TOPS and 72 GOP/s/W for ResNet18 on a cost-effective AMD Kintex UltraScale+ FPGA, while maintaining modest accuracy degradation.

02

The system applies hierarchical optimization across model parallelism, computation–communication orchestration, and low-level kernel execution, then adds OR-focused CPT and SFT data pipelines.

Abstract

Full-parameter post-training of trillion-parameter-scale MoE models introduces substantial system-level challenges for large-scale distributed training, including severe memory pressure, non-overlapped communication overhead, and inefficient kernel execution. While most large-scale LLM training systems are built around GPU-based clusters, this report presents an end-to-end optimization practice on the Ascend NPU SuperPOD. Using the DeepSeek-V4 model family as the target workload, we develop a hierarchical optimization framework spanning model-level parallelism, computation-communication orchestration, and low-level kernel execution. The resulting system achieves 34.22% Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) with a 2.93x improvement over the open-source baseline recipe while maintaining training stability. Building on this optimized infrastructure, we further establish a CPT and SFT workflow for complex Operations Research (OR) tasks. We refer to the integrated framework as SLAI T-Rex. Using DeepSeek-V4-Flash, we develop OR-oriented CPT and SFT data pipelines that combine collected domain resources with solver-verified synthetic optimization documents. The resulting dataset contains 10K high-quality SFT samples spanning four task categories and three problem representations. The specialized model achieves the highest average zero-shot Pass@1 score among the evaluated models, reaching 71.81% and outperforming GPT-5.4-Mini and the base DeepSeek-V4-Flash model by 3.98 and 11.27 percentage points, respectively. Overall, this work demonstrates a full-stack pathway from efficient trillion-parameter model post-training on Ascend infra to domain-specialized Flash models for solver-grounded mathematical modeling, advancing frontier-model systems for complex reasoning.

Odin: Primitive-Level Synchronization for Distributed Point-Based Neural Rendering

CategoryAreaTraining Systems / Parallel and Distributed TrainingTopiclarge-scale pretraining systems
Zhenxiang Ma, Zeyu He, Yuanzhen Zhou, Zhenyu Yang, Yuchang Zhang, Miao Tao et al.
high · 2026-07-22

Why it matters Odin changes synchronization in distributed point-based rendering from task or iteration scope to the primitive scope, targeting the barrier stalls exposed when optimized renderers make per-view computation cheap. It is relevant to systems with sparse, view-dependent mutable state: the paper reports 1.22x average throughput and 82% of critical-path wait hidden on 8 GPUs, plus up to 1.89x over Grendel at 64 GPUs without changing renderer kernels, optimizers, training budgets, or model capacity.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

View-dependent primitive updates make global task and iteration barriers a major source of waiting in distributed point-based rendering training.

02
Method

An ahead-of-time scheduler finds low-conflict overlap windows, while the runtime validates primitive publication before later work reads mutable state.

03
Difference

The system synchronizes individual primitives rather than whole tasks or iterations and admits only low-impact delayed reads when gradient evidence supports them.

04
Evidence

Experiments across four pipelines, 13 scenes, and 8 GPUs report 1.22x average throughput and 82% of critical-path wait hidden.

Abstract

Point-based neural rendering (PBNR) represents 3D scenes as explicit, trainable primitives and underpins high-quality reconstruction and emerging embodied AI and world-model pipelines. Unlike layer-structured neural networks, PBNR has primitive-indexed dependencies: each view reads and updates only a sparse, view-dependent subset of mutable scene state. As large scenes require distributed training and optimized renderers reduce per-view computation, global task- or iteration-level barriers increasingly place synchronization, rather than rendering, on the critical path. We present Odin, a distributed PBNR training system that replaces global barriers with primitive-level synchronization. Its ahead-of-time scheduler uses stable locality and phase order to identify low-conflict overlap windows, while the runtime validates primitive publication before later work observes mutable state. Odin provides a quality-first path that preserves synchronized-training visibility and a throughput-first path that uses overlap and gradient evidence to admit only small, low-impact delayed reads; structural changes and high-impact cases remain synchronized. Across four existing PBNR pipelines and 13 non-city scenes on 8 GPUs, Odin improves throughput by 1.22 times on average and hides 82% of critical-path wait while preserving reconstruction quality. In a MatrixCity mixed-parallel case study scaling to 64 GPUs, Odin improves throughput over Grendel by up to 1.89 times without changing renderer kernels, optimizers, training budgets, or model capacity.

The efficient and scalable integration of quantum resources into high-performance computing (HPC) environments requires standardized mechanisms for resource management, scheduling, and workflow orchestration across diverse and heterogeneous infrastructures. The Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI) addresses this challenge through a thin, vendor-agnostic middleware layer that provides standardized APIs for scheduling, executing, and monitoring quantum workloads while exposing quantum resources as first-class schedulable resources alongside CPUs and GPUs. Although previous work demonstrated QRMI integration with the Slurm workload manager, its applicability across other workload managers remained unexamined. This paper extends the validation of QRMI to a broad range of workload managers, including PBS, LSF, Grid Engine, Kubernetes, and the Flux Framework, encompassing traditional batch schedulers, a cloud-native orchestration platform, and a graph-based scheduler. We examine the integration patterns, implementation requirements, and scheduler-specific considerations associated with each environment and compare QRMI with alternative approaches to quantum resource integration. We demonstrate that QRMI provides a portable and flexible abstraction layer that minimizes scheduler-specific modifications while enabling consistent access to heterogeneous quantum resources across both on-premises and cloud environments.

Method brief
01
Problem

Iterative NTT accelerators are constrained by ping-pong memories and large memory blocks tied to the cyclotomic ring size.

02
Method

The design uses four n/4-sized memories, multiplication-free inverse-NTT rescaling, and two pipelined unified Cooley-Tukey and Gentleman-Sande butterfly units.

03
Difference

It replaces conventional large-memory organization with parallel banking while preserving total memory capacity and supporting both butterfly directions in a unified unit.

04
Evidence

FPGA experiments report 2.67x and 1.48x higher average Area-Time Product efficiency than the cited area-optimized and high-speed accelerator baselines.

Abstract

The iterative forward and inverse number theoretic transform (NTT) is a key component in lattice-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC), typically implemented using Cooley-Tukey and Gentleman-Sande butterfly units. Existing iterative NTT accelerators often rely on ping-pong memory schemes and large memory blocks tied to the cyclotomic ring, which limits overall efficiency. To overcome this, we propose a memory-parallelization strategy using four smaller n/4-sized memories for ring size n, preserving the total memory footprint of conventional designs. We also introduce a multiplication-free rescaling architecture for the inverse NTT. Building on these innovations, we perform a comprehensive hardware-based design space exploration of unified Cooley-Tukey and Gentleman-Sande butterfly units, evaluating both coarse- and fine-grained pipelining strategies. The resulting optimized butterfly unit forms the core of our proposed pipelined and memory-parallelized NTT accelerator, "PIP-NTT". It integrates two such units alongside the memory-parallelization scheme to boost computational throughput under tight area constraints. Experimental results on FPGA platforms show that PIP-NTT achieves 2.67x and 1.48x higher efficiency in average Area-Time Product compared to the most area-optimized and high-speed NTT accelerators in the literature. The design is scalable across butterfly radices and adaptable to other PQC schemes, making it a versatile solution for future cryptographic hardware
